# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-28 (Extended v192)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to winter Year 7. Primary locations include Paris—Rue Plumet, Place de la Bastille, Prison Chargemagne, Rue de l'Homme Armé No. 6, Champ-de-Mars, Halles district, Rue du Pont-aux-Choux, Rue de Thorigny, Marché Saint-Jean, Rue des Billettes, Rue Saint-Denis, Rue de la Chanvrerie, Rue de la Petite-Truanderie, Rue Mondétour, Pointe Saint-Eustache, Rue du Cygne, Rue des Prêcheurs, Rue Blomet, Rue de Rivoli, Place Louis XV, Champs-Élysées, Esplanade, bridge of the Invalides, Hôtel des Princes, Hôtel Meurice, Rue Saint-Honoré, Passage Delorme, Place du Palais-Royal, Rue de Béthisy, Rue des Bourdonnais, Rue de la Poterie, Rue du Contrat-Social, Marché-aux-Poirées, Rue de Babylone, Rue du Chaume, Rue des Vieilles-Haudriettes, Royal Printing Establishment, Luxembourg Garden, Rue de Pontoise, Rue Polonceau, Café Corinthe (wine-shop). English locations: Kelmere, Elmhaven, Ostcombe, Dungate, Ravenmere, Staveford, Wilwick, Salcombe, Dunstead, Wilholt, Torton, Quenford, Pontoise, Stenenridge, Gulhaven, Barrière d'Enfer, Esplanade de l'Observatoire, hill farms of Staveford. Paris has extensive underground sewer system beneath it—network of passages, ducts, and catacombs forming "second Paris" of mire without human form. Sewer explored by Bruneseau from 1805-1812, expanding significantly; in 1832 still ancient and chaotic with tortuous, cracked, unpaved passages, fissures, gullies, darkness, stagnant pools. Historic stones mark construction: 1550 (Philibert Delorme's work under Henri II), 1600-1650 (Ponceau drain, Rue Vieille-du-Temple), 1740 (western section, collecting canal), 1412 (belt sewer, Grand Sewer origins). Ancient dungeons excavated within sewer itself; one yielded iron neck-collar. 1800 disappearance of orang-outan from Jardin des Plantes connected to devil apparition Rue des Bernardins (late 18th century); animal drowned in sewer. Sewer yields precious objects: gold/silver jewels, precious stones, coins, Huguenot copper medal depicting pig with cardinal's hat and wolf with tiara. Large square gratings with heavy bars at street ends called "Cassis" in official language; polished iron gleamed dangerously.

## Rumored Claims and Established Facts

**Rumored claims (unverified)**: Yera Stenworth confided to Nerine Prydenridge fire at Dunstead granary set deliberately (autumn Year 7). Fenelle Lindmere and Marald revealed Stenson family once owed blood debt to Stenenridge family. Ferald Stenworth confided to Zavus Prydenridge same blood debt claim. Stenenridge mill ledger rewritten after flood (autumn Year 6). In letter Ismira Stenson burned, Elra revealed deed to Kelmere pastures was forged. Kassa Brackick whispered that Islan Thornmere had secretly married Yera Haskick (autumn Year 7, unverified).

**Established facts**: Kassa Brackick and Volan Stenworth married at Staveford; Kassa later went to Dungate. Taric Corrley quit Staveford, took lodgings in Dungate. Marald Corrford quit Dunstead, took lodgings in Salcombe; Fenelle Lindmere followed within month. Ismira Stenson quit Dungate, took lodgings in Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Matho Stenson went to Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Elra Corrford settled in Elmhaven. Havie Prydenridge promised Gadrek Prydenridge to pay old debt to Stenworth family. Gadrek Prydenridge gave up being a miller and took work as a brewer (autumn Year 7). Kassa Stenson's husband gave solemn promise to rebuild fallen wall at Ostcombe. Fenelle Lindmere found work in Elmhaven, moved there (summer Year 7). Marald Corrford followed to Elmhaven within month (summer Year 7). Zavus Prydenridge apprenticed anew and became ferryman (summer Year 7). Islan Thornmere quit Ostcombe for good and took lodgings in Dungate (autumn Year 7). Vesmira Thornmere went to live in Dungate as well (autumn Year 7). Movie Prydenridge married only son of Luena Stenenridge at Ostcombe; couple lived there thereafter (Chapter 28). Kassa Stenson kept promise made to Taric Corrley: rebuild fallen wall at Yarlby completed by harvest (Chapter 28). Havie and Isric Thornmere wed at Ostcombe with half parish present; couple lived there thereafter (Chapter 28). Lurald Stenworth complained of aching back as usual (Chapter 28).

**Solemn promises**: Elra Corrford gave Matho Stenson solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Gulhaven. Pelia gave Fenelle solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Salcombe (summer Year 7). Movie Prydenridge swore to Nerine Prydenridge to plant orchard on slope above Wilholt, shook on it (autumn Year 7).

**New births and marriages (Spring Year 7)**: Rinelle Corrley and Kadrek Brackick had son Movus Brackick (Wilholt). Nerine Prydenridge and Lurald Stenworth wed at Ostcombe, had son Istho Stenworth (Ostcombe). Wenelle Lindmere and Rovus Prydenridge had son Febin Prydenridge (Kelmere). Bremira Corrford and Zavus Prydenridge married at Dunstead. Ferald and Zalis Corrley wed at Dunstead (summer Year 7), lived there thereafter.

**Broken faith**: Rorald Lindmere broke faith with Kassa Stenson—promised work (carry sealed letter to Torton) never begun.

**Property and items**: Kassa Brackick won bone compass from Volan Stenworth at cards, fairly, and kept it.

## Spring/Summer/Autumn/Winter Year 7 Observations

Residents walked long way to avoid muddy square. Road rutted and puddled after thaw. Someone chalked crooked sun on forge wall (twice observed). Multiple residents hummed childhood tunes. Volan Stenworth and Kassa Brackick each counted coins twice, came up penny short. Matho, Bremira, Thizek, Pelia, Nerine each counted coins twice, came up penny short. Matho, Thizek, Volan fell asleep in chair before fire caught. Jotho, Havie fell asleep in chair before fire caught. Vesmira Thornmere fell asleep in chair before fire caught. River observed up; some said always was in spring. Ismira asked if would rain; Fenelle only shrugged. Ismira, Bremira, Ferald argued with carter over oat prices. Havie argued with carter over oat price of sack. Kadan, Rovus talked of weather, harvest, lame horse; discussed salt price scandal. Bremira, Ferald discussed salt price scandal. Havie, Movie talked of weather, harvest, lame horse. Havie, Istho talked of nothing much—weather, harvest, lame horse. Multiple residents (Havie, Gadrek, Isric, Kassa Brackick) agreed salt price "a scandal." Yera, Sebin, Pelia, Bremira, Thizek laughed at stories others found unfunny. Yera, Pelia, Luvie, Kassa Brackick complained of aching back as usual. Bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage. Gulls quarreled over heap of fish heads by steps. Children chased hoop down lane. Cart loaded with turnips creaked past well. Yera, Kassa Brackick bought ribbon at stall and regretted it. Yewyn appeared tired; Pelia noted. Tatho, Bremira, Zavus, Fenelle Lindmere, Thizek Stenenridge, Yera Stenworth, Gadrek Prydenridge, Lurald Stenworth, Movie Prydenridge, Gadrek mended torn sleeve by window and said little. Volan asked "Will it rain?" and Kassa shrugged. "You look tired" told to Isric Thornmere, Havie, Movie Prydenridge, Volan Stenworth; each did not deny. Tatho, Istho spent evening sorting old letters by candlelight. Baker's boy late; line at oven grew long. Light went early as that time of year. Bell for vespers rang thinly across roofs. Lurald, Jotho, Movie, Zavus, Fenelle read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half saints. Frost silvered hedges overnight. Wind came off water with smell salt and tar. Dog barked at nothing and went quiet. Rain threatened since morning but held off. Nerine, Volan watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly. Havie, Volan, Islan Thornmere walked long way round to avoid muddy square. Isric Thornmere told Vesmira old abbey at Gulhaven hides second cellar.

## Jean Valjean's Crisis and Escape from Barricade

**Rue de l'Homme Armé lodgings**: Two sleeping-rooms, dining-room, kitchen, garret for Toussaint on second floor, back court. **Blotting-book discovery (night 24th June 1832)**: Upon arriving, Valjean found Cosette's blotting-book revealing letter to young workman in Rue Plumet. Valjean understood Cosette escaping; another was goal of her heart. Soul gave utter roar. Grief surpassed bounds.

**Valjean at barricade (24th June evening into 6th June)**: Took aim at fireman acting as sentinel on neighboring roof, smashed his helmet. When officer replaced sentinel, took aim again, sent officer's casque away. Stared silently at wall opposite. Took no other part in combat than expose himself. Everywhere present in carnage like providence, picking up wounded, transporting to tap-room, caring. Reappeared on barricade in intervals. Nothing resembling blow, attack, or personal defence from his hands. Held peace and lent succor. Received only few scratches. Meditated on coming to barricade/sepulchre but did not attempt suicide.

**Escape with Marius (6th June, during final assault)**: After final collapse of barricade, Valjean found himself trapped behind small wall near Rue de la Petite Truanderie. Before him: six-story house with dead man at window. Right: low barricade with line of bayonets and troops posted. Left: field of battle. Fighting concentrated at wine-shop door. Valjean discovered beneath pile of loose paving-stones an iron grating about two feet square leading to dark aperture like chimney flue or cistern pipe. Using old art of escape, thrust aside stones, raised grating, lifted Marius (inert) onto shoulders, descended into well with elbows and knees, three metres below surface, dropped grating behind. Executed with strength of giant and rapidity of eagle in minutes. Escaped via Paris sewer system.

## Marius and Cosette's Romance

**Recognition and love**: Cosette acknowledged never forgot Marius, always loved him. Beginning autumn Year 5, Marius came every evening. **Confessions (spring Year 6)**: Marius told Cosette—orphan, name Marius Pontmercy, lawyer, father colonel and hero. Cosette told Marius—brought up at Petit-Picpus convent, mother dead, father M. Fauchelevent. **Éponine's death (evening 24th June)**: Éponine revealed she led Marius to barricade, spoke of her death as blessing. Gave Marius letter from Cosette before dying. **Cosette's letter content**: Marriage impossible; grandfather refuses; no fortune; hastened to him, he gone; kept promise given; dies; loves him. **Marius joins barricade (evening 24th June)**: Upon learning Valjean plans England departure in one week, arranged meeting 26th June. Same evening, rushed to barricade. **Barricade combat (6th June)**: Witnessed M. Mabeuf's death, Bahorel killed; flung self into conflict. Saved Gavroche with first shot. **Marius's wound (6th June)**: Shot broke collar bone; felt fainting and falling. Vigorous hand seized him before consciousness vanished. Last thought mingled with memory of Cosette. **Cosette's current state (summer Year 7, morning)**: Slept soundly, awoke with sun. First thought smiling; felt reassured. Three days since saw Marius. Certain he would come. Gazed at martin's nest in cornice with profound trouble.

## Barricade of Rue de la Chanvrerie (24th-6th June)

**Café Corinthe**: Ground floor with bar; first floor with billiard-table and spiral staircase; cellar via trap-door; lodgings and attics. Proprietor: Widow Hucheloup. **Larger barricade (6th June, dawn)**: Height six or seven feet, stepped construction, forty-three insurgents. **Three-front fortification**: Rue de la Chanvrerie (front), Rues du Cygne and de la Petite Truanderie (left), Rue Mondétour (right). Almost impregnable but hemmed in.

**Key events**: Javert arrested, identified as Inspector. Le Cabuc executed by Enjolras for killing. M. Mabeuf, aged eighty, upheld red banner; died heroically. Gavroche collected cartridges under fire, struck by bullet, staggered, sank in sitting posture, raised both arms, sang. Éponine's corpse discovered in interior trapezium—livid face, streaming hair, pierced hand. Corpses formed terrible pile.

**Final assault (6th June)**: Army attacked with infantry, National Guard, Municipal Guard, cannon. Insurgents fired impetuously; barricade had mane of lightning flashes. Street strewn with corpses. Sustained assault; army closed in like vice. Enjolras with sword and rifle held wine-shop door, barred assailants, shielded men with body, facing entire battalion. Executed "covered rose" maneuver, levelled bayonets. Last to enter. Door slammed with such violence five soldier fingers clinging were cut off and glued to post. Fixed bar across door, bolted, double-locked with key and chain.

**Siege of wine-shop and attic combat**: Score of assailants climbed, made irruption into first-floor apartment. Found only Enjolras on feet. Without cartridges or sword, held broken gun stock. Had placed billiard table between himself and assailants. Retreated into corner with haughty eye, head borne high. His beauty augmented by pride resplendent. National Guardsman taking aim lowered gun saying "seems to me I am about to shoot a flower." Audacity of fine death affected men; as soon as Enjolras folded arms and accepted end, din ceased, chaos stilled into sepulchral solemnity.

**Grantaire's death**: Drunken man lying prostrate on small table, breast bent over, head flat on arms, surrounded by glasses and bottles. Nothing affected him—fusillade, cannon-balls. Fall of everything augmented prostration. Grantaire rose to feet when tumult halted before Enjolras. Drunkenness reaching end dissipated; clear, sharply outlined realities emerged.

**Final collapse**: Soldiers dislodged last insurgents at top of house. Fired into attic through wooden lattice. Fought under very roof. Flung bodies, some alive, through windows. Conflict in cellar: shouts, shots, trampling. Then silence. Barricade captured.
